clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote daily to her sister; Walter spent long hours out in the trees and distanced from June; Glen fought at school and was sent home twice; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan over a quarrel about their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks; Walter and June fought over money for new trees; and by September, June had joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, her anxiety easing. These shifts in the family sit close together from spring 1952 through early autumn 1953, marking the family's adjustment to the move and the strains it brought between Walter and June and in Glen's schooling.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, within a year: Walter drank heavily; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working; and by October, Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning other men's trees. The period reaches from the failure through the autumn when Walter's functioning recovered, holding the shifts that rippled through the household as the men clashed and the children reacted.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975, within a year and a half: Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck in the yard for hours; he and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and distanced from Marian; Walter drank again after six years sober; and by June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team. The period holds shifts across the household as Glen's loss of work brought conflict between him and Marian, Nora withdrew, and Walter's old symptom returned, settling as Glen found work driving a delivery truck.

clusters.name: Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into the house in January 1990, within eighteen months: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis fought most nights; and by the summer of 1991, after Wilma took a flat in town in June, Nora's eczema cleared. The period marks the disruption brought by three generations in one house, with Nora caught between Hollis and his mother, her children reacting, and her own symptom rising and falling with the household's shift.
